newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal will not fund Nobel laureate's Timor plan.
newsitem.headline: Portugal will not fund Nobel laureate's Timor plan.

text.p: Portugal will not fund a special foundation planned by Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta to help anti-Indonesia activists in its former East Timor colony, but will continue humanitarian aid, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
"We will continue to offer humanitarian aid but on a case-by-case basis," the spokesman told Reuters.
Indonesia annexed the eastern half of the island in 1976 after a bloody invasion but its action has never been recognised by the United Nations.
The government decision, taken after consultations with opposition parties on Wednesday, was aimed at getting Lisbon out of a diplomatic impasse.

Ramos-Horta, who was jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize last month with East Timor Roman Catholic bishop Carlos Belo for their efforts on behalf of the East Timorese, has announced his intention to use his share of the $1.2 million award to set up the foundation in Lisbon.
He suggested on a recent visit that Portugal, which is still recognised as the territory's administrator by the United Nations, should help finance the venture.

But the government, which has been holding regular U.N-sponsored contacts with Indonesia about the troubled territory, feared that Jakarta could seize on any direct financial aid as a reason to break off the talks.
Ramos-Horta is the international spokesman for jailed resistance leader Xanana Gusmao, whose movement has a guerrilla arm still active in East Timor.
